What does a plant need in order to grow?
Water only, without sunlight or soil
Sunlight, water, and soil
Sunlight only, without water from the soil
Dry soil without water or light
A plant needs light, water, minerals from soil, and air to grow well.
Leaves take in light; roots take in water and minerals.
Without enough light or water, a plant can weaken and die.
Which part of a plant absorbs water from the soil?
The leaves — they collect water that falls from rain.
The stem — it holds the plant upright but does not absorb water from the soil.
The roots — they absorb water and minerals from the soil.
The lower part of the stem in the soil — it absorbs water just like roots do.

Roots grow underground and absorb water and dissolved minerals from the soil. The water then travels up through the stem to reach the leaves and other parts of the plant. Without roots taking in water, the plant would dry out and die.
Roots anchor the plant in the soil and absorb the water and nutrients it needs to grow.
Water travels from the roots through the stem and into the leaves, where it is used for photosynthesis.
What is photosynthesis?
A process in which a plant breaks sugar apart using oxygen for energy
A process in which a plant makes food from light, water, and carbon dioxide
A process in which a plant loses water through leaf openings on a bright day
A process that mostly happens in the stem underground
In photosynthesis, a plant uses light, water, and carbon dioxide to make sugar and release oxygen.
Photosynthesis happens in chloroplasts, mostly in leaves.
Photosynthesis supports food chains in most ecosystems.
When do plants carry out cellular respiration?
Plants respire at night and during the day
Plants respire only in daytime sunlight
Plants usually do not respire at all
Only roots respire, not leaves
Cellular respiration happens day and night. Photosynthesis happens only when there is light.
Cellular respiration releases energy from sugar.
Photosynthesis makes sugar; respiration uses that sugar for energy.
What do stomata do for a plant leaf?
They carry water from the soil directly to the leaf.
They absorb sunlight for the plant to use.
They let gases like carbon dioxide and oxygen pass in and out of the leaf.
They anchor the plant firmly in the ground.
Stomata are tiny openings on a leaf that allow gas exchange — letting carbon dioxide in and oxygen out during photosynthesis.
Light energy and water are used by the plant during photosynthesis.
Gases move in and out of leaves through stomata.
What is the state of matter of ice?
Solid
Liquid
Gas
Mixture
Ice is water in the solid state. Warming ice turns it into liquid water.
Water can be solid (ice), liquid (water), or gas (water vapor).
Changing temperature can change the state of matter.
Which statement about metals is true?
They insulate electricity better than plastic and wood
They usually conduct heat and electricity well
They are transparent to light like thin glass
They break easily and cannot be bent or flattened
Metals often conduct heat and electricity, which is why they are used in wires and cookware.
Many metals are shiny and can be hammered into sheets or drawn into wires.
Not every metal is equally strong, but many are tough and durable.
Which statement about plastic is true?
Plastic is made in factories and is not found ready-made in nature
Plastic is found in nature the way rock is
Plastic is a kind of wood
Plastic is made only from sand
Plastic is manufactured, often from petroleum. It is not a natural material like wood or stone.
Natural materials come from living things or Earth's nonliving materials.
Synthetic materials are made through industrial processes.
A solution of salt and water is an example of which kind of mixture?
A heterogeneous mixture
A homogeneous mixture
A pure chemical compound
A usually flammable gas
When salt dissolves in water, the mixture looks the same throughout. That is a homogeneous mixture.
A homogeneous mixture looks uniform, with no clear boundaries between parts.
A solution is a mixture in which one material dissolves in another.
What is a physical change?
A change that creates a completely new substance
A change in which matter changes form or state but stays the same substance
A change that can happen only with very strong heating
A change that happens only to metals
In a physical change, shape or state can change, but the chemical identity stays the same.
Melting ice into water is a physical change—it is still water.
Burning paper is a chemical change because new materials form.
What causes day and night on Earth?
The Sun moves around Earth once every 24 hours.
Earth spins on its own axis, so different parts face the Sun at different times.
The Moon blocks sunlight from reaching Earth at night.
Earth moves closer to and farther from the Sun each day.
Day and night are caused by Earth rotating on its axis. The side facing the Sun experiences day; the side facing away experiences night.
Earth completes one full rotation every 24 hours.
As Earth spins, each part moves from sunlight into shadow and back again.
Which statement about Earth is true?
Earth is orbited by the Sun, not by the Moon.
Earth orbits the Sun once every year.
Earth stays completely still in space.
A full day-and-night cycle on Earth takes 48 hours.
Earth travels around the Sun once each year. This yearly orbit, combined with Earth's tilt, gives us seasons. Earth also spins on its axis every 24 hours, giving us day and night.
Earth orbits the Sun in a path called a revolution, which takes about 365 days.
Earth also rotates on its own axis, causing day and night.
Which statement about the Moon is true?
The Moon reflects light from the Sun — it does not produce its own light.
The Moon is a planet that orbits the Sun directly.
The Moon produces its own bright light every single night.
The Moon shines with equal brightness from every direction at all times.
The Moon is not a star or a planet — it is a natural satellite that orbits Earth. It does not generate its own light. The moonlight we see is actually sunlight bouncing off the Moon's surface.
Stars, like the Sun, produce their own light through nuclear reactions.
The Moon is a rocky body that only reflects sunlight, which is why it can appear bright at night.
Which statement about Earth's layers is true?
Earth is only a thin crust over empty space
Earth is made of a crust, a mantle, and a core
Earth is one single uniform layer
We have no information about Earth's interior
Earth has a thin outer crust, a thick mantle, and a very hot core.
Much of what we know about Earth's interior comes from earthquakes and geologic study.
The inner core is dense and extremely hot.
Which action helps protect the environment?
Sorting at home, then dumping everything into one public bin
Using less paper but throwing all plastic in regular trash
Recycling paper, plastic, and glass in the right bins
Crushing bottles to save space without recycling them
Recycling reduces waste, saves raw materials, and helps protect the environment.
Protecting the environment includes reducing waste, recycling, and saving resources.
Recycling lets useful materials be made into new products.
What is an ecosystem?
A collection of human buildings with no living nature
Living things together with their surroundings and the links between them
Only museum samples with no living environment
A city building diagram with no plants, animals, or food links
An ecosystem includes living things, their habitat, and how they interact—for food, shelter, and more.
Examples include a forest, a pond, and a coral reef.
A change in the environment can affect every part of the ecosystem.
Which statement about air pollution is true?
Air pollution can also affect human health
Air pollution affects only plants
Air pollution is not related to health
Only polluted water usually harms people
Air pollution can harm the lungs and lead to other health problems.
Common sources include traffic, industry, and burning fuels.
Reducing air pollution helps people and nature.
Which statement about greenhouse gases is true?
They are rare in nature and do not affect Earth's warmth at all
They trap heat in the atmosphere, and their amount affects climate
They gather only above countries with tall mountains
They come mainly from volcanoes with no link to people
Gases such as carbon dioxide and methane trap heat. Too much of them warms the planet.
A natural greenhouse effect helps keep Earth warm enough for life.
Human activity has added large amounts of greenhouse gases to the air.
Two identical containers of water are left out — one in the sun and one in the shade. Which will lose more water, and why?
The one in the shade, because shade slows down water loss.
They will lose the same amount of water because air temperature is the same everywhere.
The one in the sun, because heat from the sun causes water to evaporate faster.
The one in the sun will actually gain more water from sunlight.
Heat from the sun gives water molecules extra energy, causing them to evaporate more quickly from the container in the sun.
Heat energy transfers from a hot body to a cooler one.
More heat means faster evaporation from water surfaces.
What is important to do at the start of every science experiment?
Decide the 'right' result first so the experiment matches it
Write a clear question or problem you want to test
Change several variables at once to get a bigger result
Skip planning and start measuring right away
A science experiment begins with a clear question. Then you plan the steps to investigate it.
Science is built on questions, observations, and experiments.
Careful notes make it easier to compare results.
What is a controlled variable in an experiment?
A factor that is kept the same in every trial to make the test fair.
A measurement that changes randomly each time it is taken.
A prediction written at the beginning of the experiment.
The final number recorded at the end of the experiment.

A controlled variable is any condition you keep the same throughout all trials so it does not affect your results. Only the one variable you are testing should change. For example, if you are testing how much water affects plant growth, the amount of sunlight and soil type should stay the same in every pot.
Controlled variables make an experiment fair by removing hidden causes.
The variable you change on purpose is called the independent variable.
Put the stages of the water cycle in order from first to last:
Evaporation → condensation → precipitation → collection in water sources
Condensation → collection → evaporation → precipitation
Collection → precipitation → condensation → evaporation
Precipitation → evaporation → condensation → collection
Water evaporates, forms clouds by condensation, falls as rain or snow, then gathers in oceans, lakes, and groundwater.
The water cycle moves water among ocean, land, and atmosphere.
The Sun, wind, and land shape all help drive the cycle.
What is found near the top of a plant?
Roots
Leaves
Flowers
Fruits
Leaves grow on the upper parts of a plant, above the stem, where they can take in sunlight.
A plant has roots below, a stem in the middle, and leaves and flowers above.
Leaves look green because they contain chlorophyll.
What is found at the bottom of a plant?
Roots grow in the soil. They hold the plant in place and take in water and minerals.
Roots grow down into the ground.
Roots help the plant stand steady.
What happens to a plant if it has no water?
It keeps growing for a long time if it has lots of light
It wilts and becomes weak
Its leaves stay upright and green for a long time without water
It stops respiring until water returns
Water is essential. Without it, a plant wilts, leaves dry out, and the plant may die.
Water helps a plant stay alive and strong.
Roots take water from the soil.
Water, light, air, and materials from the soil
A plant can grow with no sunlight at all
A place with lots of people nearby
Only a place that has water
